sections.title: Cell and habitat
sections.text: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii is a unicellular green alga from freshwater and moist soils, best known as a laboratory model organism. A cell is about 10 μm across; two anterior flagella allow it to swim. A large cup-shaped chloroplast contains a pyrenoid, and an eyespot contributes to light sensing.

sections.title: Microscopic plate
sections.text: This alga has no leaves, flowers, roots or fruits. The plate greatly enlarges the cells and illustrates their two flagella, chloroplast and eyespot; it is explanatory and not to the scale of a plant visible to the naked eye. No reliable human food use is included.
